verdicts.summary: The new clause only blocks arming a child that is not armed yet. In the usual order the child hits the limit first, the sweep arms it within one tick, and the parent settles later. Settling does not disarm the child, so at reset the child still auto-resumes and wakes the settled parent. That is the hazard this commit set out to fix.
verdicts.scenario: 1) autoResumeLimitedThreads is on. Parent P starts subagent C. 2) C's run fails with usage_limit and resetAt T+5h. The turn-item error event invalidates the DueHint (UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts:88). On the next tick P is not settled, so C passes the fresh-arm branch and autoArmLimitRecovery writes limitRecovery {runId, resetAt, autoResume:true} (Orchestrator.ts:13971-13998). 3) P then settles: the user settles it, P's own agent does via settleAfterRun (ThreadManagementService.ts:1032-1041), or auto-settle runs (Orchestrator.ts:13006-13035). The thread.settle reducer (Orchestrator.ts:3485-3504) changes only P's fields; C's limitRecovery is untouched. 4) At T+5h C matches the first OR branch (ProjectionStore.ts:3958-3967), which has no parent check. limitRecoveryCommand returns message.dispatch 'Continue where you left off.' (UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts:57-78). C resumes and wakes P. The new test asserts this exact behaviour (ProjectionStore.test.ts diff lines 157-190).
verdicts.consequence: A settled parent is still woken by its subagent's auto-resume whenever the child was armed before the parent settled. That is the normal order, because arming happens on the next scheduler tick after the failure. The fix only works when the parent settled before the child hit the limit.
